title: Gauss–Markov and BLUE
dek: Among linear unbiased estimators of Xβ, OLS has the smallest variance when errors are uncorrelated with equal variance. That is a small kingdom.
story: Gauss–Markov: if E[ε | X] = 0 and Var(ε | X) = σ² I, then OLS is BLUE — best linear unbiased estimator of any linear functional cᵀβ. “Best” means smallest variance in the class of estimators that are linear in Y and unbiased.

The theorem does not say OLS is maximum likelihood (that needs Gaussianity). It does not say OLS is best among nonlinear estimators (James–Stein, ridge, lasso live outside the class). It does not say the coefficient is causal (that is E[ε | X] as a structural residual, a different fight).

When Var(ε | X) is not spherical — heteroskedasticity, clustering — OLS can remain unbiased for the linear projection and stop being BLUE. GLS, mixed models, or sandwich SEs are the three usual responses, and they are not interchangeable.
deep: Linearity here means E[Y | X] = Xβ, or at least that you are targeting the population linear projection. Unbiasedness of β̂ needs E[Xᵀε] = 0, which follows from E[ε | X] = 0.
No multicollinearity in the theorem’s unique-BLUE form: X full column rank. Near-collinearity does not break unbiasedness; it inflates Var(β̂) = σ² (XᵀX)⁻¹.
Normality is not on the list. It enters for exact t and F, and for MLE = OLS. Large-n Wald tests can proceed with sandwich SEs without Gaussian ε.

If you add a random effect, you have left the BLUE-for-OLS theorem and entered GLS: the BLUE is (Xᵀ V⁻¹ X)⁻¹ Xᵀ V⁻¹ Y for known V. Estimating V is why mixed-model SEs need care (REML, Kenward–Roger, Bayes).

example.title: Heteroskedastic MIC by dose
example.setup: log MIC vs dose. Residual scatter fans out at high dose (variance grows). OLS line still estimates the linear projection. Model-based SEs using s² (XᵀX)⁻¹ do not.

steps.title: What survives
steps.body: If E[log MIC | dose] is linear, β̂_dose remains consistent. Gauss–Markov’s “best” is gone because Var(ε|X) ≠ σ² I.

steps.title: What to print
steps.body: Sandwich SE, or WLS with a variance model, or a GLM with a better V(μ). Do not quote the default OLS t as if GM still applied.

steps.title: What not to claim
steps.body: BLUE is not a causal badge. Even with spherical errors, dose was not randomised in this notebook.

example.takeaway: Name the class: projection, BLUE, MLE, or causal. Gauss–Markov is only the second.

check.prompt: Gauss–Markov says OLS is best among:
choices: All estimators, including ridge and Bayes
Linear unbiased estimators, when errors are spherical and mean-zero given X
check.answer: Linear unbiased estimators, when errors are spherical and mean-zero given X
check.why: The class is small on purpose. Shrinkage estimators can beat OLS in MSE by leaving the unbiased class.

whyWrong.All estimators, including ridge and Baye: Those are outside the linear unbiased class.
whyWrong.All consistent estimators: Too big a class; no uniformly best.
whyWrong.Causal estimators in DAGs: GM is not a causal theorem.
